metadata.title: Warehouse Audit Working Pack
metadata.intendedUse: Plan a scoped warehouse review, record evidence and carry findings through to action and verification.
metadata.scopeLimit: The 28 starter checks need the requirements, goods, activities and operating conditions of your review. They do not provide a complete legal or sector-specific audit, certification or an overall pass score.
metadata.examplesNote: Examples are fictional and separate from blank working records.

instructions.title: Start with the decision
instructions.text: Record the question this review must answer, the areas to examine and who will use the findings. You can plan evidence before making observations.

instructions.title: Establish the criteria
instructions.text: Name the applicable procedure, agreement or other requirement and its version. Assign it to the relevant check. Write 'Not yet established' where it is unknown.

instructions.title: Keep the sample visible
instructions.text: Record the goods, locations, shifts, period and transactions examined. Keep exclusions and evidence limits with the conclusion.

instructions.title: Use evidence references
instructions.text: Enter short observations and record references. Use roles and site aliases where sufficient; avoid copying customer details or sensitive records into the pack.

instructions.title: Leave uncertainty open
instructions.text: A blank status means Not reviewed. Record missing criteria, conflicting accounts and unanswered questions. Label a possible cause as a hypothesis.

instructions.title: Assign the next step
instructions.text: Give each concern an action owner, target date and verification plan. Keep the person doing the work separate from anyone who must approve resources or make a decision.

instructions.title: Separate completion from effectiveness
instructions.text: Record what was completed, then what the follow-up check showed. Work completed without effectiveness evidence remains awaiting verification.

instructions.title: Adapt the working record
instructions.text: Save a copy before entering your review. Keep the starter check IDs and add local checks where needed. The examples illustrate recording; they are not findings about your operation.

statuses.meaning: No assessment recorded. Plan the evidence still needed.
Your evidence supports the check within the stated scope. Name the criterion and supporting reference; missing support remains a gap.
Record the observation, requirement and evidence, then assign follow-up. Do not assume the cause is established.
The available information does not settle the question. Preserve the uncertainty and request the next evidence.
Explain why the check falls outside this review. A missing reason remains an unresolved scope gap.

examples.title: Repeated inventory discrepancy
examples.label: Fictional worked example — correction and limited verification recorded
examples.purpose: Follow one evidenced stock difference through correction, a process action and verification. Keep older recurrences unresolved.

scope.decision: What explains the recurring difference, and what action should follow?
scope.operatingConditions: One unit dispatched on 5 October at 16:40. Its stock issue was still pending at the count.
scope.sample: SKU104, bin A01. Count/recount and transaction trail; follow-up covers 20 dispatches on 7–9 October across three shifts. Checks INV01–03.
scope.exclusions: Older discrepancies remain unexplained. This item and limited follow-up sample do not establish performance across all stock or shifts.
scope.criteria: Fictional procedure INV04 v3: post each stock issue before dispatch. Compare the same item, unit, location and time.
scope.reviewer: Inventory lead traces C104, RC104, S104, P418, D418 and Q418. Warehouse manager verifies the follow-up in V104.
scope.actionOwner: Inventory lead owns the handover change and pending-issue review, due 6 October 2026, 17:00.
scope.decisionOwner: Inventory manager authorises posting the one missing issue on 6 October 2026, 11:00.

findings.criterion: Fictional site procedure INV04 v3 requires each stock issue to be posted before dispatch.
findings.observation: At 09:00 on 6 October 2026, C104 and independent recount RC104 show 11 each of SKU104 in bin A01. Snapshot S104 shows 12.
findings.evidenceObtained: P418 and D418 record one unit leaving on 5 October at 16:40. Q418 shows that issue still pending at the count.
findings.evidenceNeeded: Investigate the separate older recurrences. This transaction trail does not explain those earlier differences.
findings.uncertainty: The unposted issue explains this one-unit difference. Why it remained pending and the causes of older recurrences are not established.
findings.possibleCause: Evidence confirms one unposted issue. It does not establish fraud or a root cause for all recurring discrepancies.
findings.nextAction: Post the single missing issue with approval. Give handover a named owner and review pending issues before release. Retain older cases for investigation.
findings.actionType: Authorised correction, corrective action and verification
findings.targetDate: 6 October 2026, 17:00, for handover ownership and the pending-issue review.
findings.urgency: Inventory manager requires the record correction and control change on 6 October. No wider urgency conclusion is made.
findings.completion: 6 October: manager approves posting at 11:00. Records then show 11. H104 records named handover ownership and pre-release pending-issue review in use by 17:00.
findings.verificationMethod: V104: compare 20 dispatches on 7–9 October across three shifts with INV04 v3. Check issue posting before release and recount the selected bin.
findings.verificationResult: Effective in the examined sample: all 20 issues posted before release and the selected bin matches. Older recurrences remain unresolved.
findings.decisionNeeded: The manager approves posting the one missing issue. No additional balance adjustment is made, which would double-count the correction.
findings.decisionOwner: Inventory manager for correction authority; inventory lead for the process action and older-case investigation.

examples.managementNote: Close this recorded correction and sampled follow-up. Keep older recurrences open. V104 supports the result only for the examined sample.

examples.title: Warehouse-provider renewal
examples.label: Fictional worked example — renewal decision remains open
examples.purpose: Bring service, storage and billing evidence to a renewal review. Show a verified credit alongside service and storage questions that remain open.

scope.decision: Renew the provider contract, request changes or seek further evidence?
scope.period: Review as at 8 October 2026. Service and billed-activity period: 1–7 October 2026.
scope.operatingConditions: Investigate the four late orders. Product acceptability remains unresolved because the 2 October condition record is missing.
scope.sample: 12 orders, goods affected by the 2 October record gap and one invoice line for 120 pallet-days. Checks FLOW03–04, GOODS02, GOODS04 and CONTROL03–04.
scope.exclusions: No conclusion on all provider qualifications or all shipments. Fictional invoice amounts exclude VAT and other lines.
scope.criteria: SLA12 v2: orders ready for 17:00 dispatch. CS2 v2: customer dry-storage requirement. Signed rate v2: £1.50 per pallet-day from 1 October.
scope.reviewer: Service lead checks order/staging/handover records. Quality lead assesses the record gap. Commercial lead reconciles billing; finance controller checks CN82.
scope.actionOwner: Service lead: report by 10 October. Quality lead: assessment by 9 October. Commercial lead: credit and contract timetable/options.
scope.decisionOwner: Logistics director requests the service plan and quality assessment on 8 October before a final renewal decision.

findings.criterion: Fictional SLA12 v2 requires the selected orders to be ready for 17:00 dispatch.
findings.observation: Four of 12 selected orders from 1–7 October 2026 were late against the agreed dispatch-readiness commitment.
findings.evidenceObtained: Order, staging and handover records for the 12 orders establish the four exceptions against SLA12 v2.
findings.evidenceNeeded: Service lead to examine staffing, workload, queues and exceptions around the four late orders and propose a supported service plan.
findings.uncertainty: The four exceptions are established within this sample. Their cause and wider service performance remain under investigation.
findings.possibleCause: Not yet established. The observed lateness does not identify a particular operating cause.
findings.nextAction: Service lead reports the evidence, remaining cause questions and proposed plan to the director by 10 October 2026.
findings.urgency: Director requires the service plan before the final renewal decision.
findings.completion: Open as at 8 October: investigation and service plan due 10 October.
findings.verificationMethod: After agreeing the plan, warehouse manager checks later order/staging/handover records against SLA12 v2. Agree coverage and timing with the plan.
findings.verificationDate: To be agreed after the service plan
findings.decisionNeeded: Director requests a service plan before final renewal. Commercial lead checks the contract timetable and available options.

findings.criterion: Fictional customer requirement CS2 v2 specifies dry storage for the affected goods.
findings.observation: The 2 October 2026 condition record is missing for the affected goods. The available evidence cannot establish acceptability.
findings.evidenceObtained: CS2 v2 and the condition-record review identify the specific 2 October gap.
findings.evidenceNeeded: Quality lead to assess the affected goods, remaining condition evidence and any action needed under CS2 v2.
findings.uncertainty: Missing evidence does not establish acceptable or unacceptable goods. Product acceptability and any disposition remain for quality assessment.
findings.nextAction: Quality lead assesses the affected goods and evidence gap under CS2 v2 and reports to the director by 9 October 2026.
findings.urgency: Director requires the quality assessment before final renewal. Quality lead determines any response needed for the goods.
findings.completion: Open as at 8 October: quality assessment due 9 October.
findings.verificationMethod: Quality lead defines any required action and evidence of its effectiveness against CS2 v2 after assessing the affected goods.
findings.verificationOwner: Quality lead; any additional assessor to be identified through the assessment.
findings.verificationDate: To be agreed after the quality assessment
findings.verificationResult: Pending — no acceptability or effectiveness conclusion
findings.decisionNeeded: Director requests the quality assessment before final renewal. Keep the condition-record gap and any product decision visible.
findings.decisionOwner: Logistics director for renewal; quality lead to establish the required product decision and authority.

findings.criterion: Signed fictional rate v2, effective 1 October 2026: £1.50 per pallet-day for the same unit and billed period.
findings.observation: Invoice bills 120 pallet-days at £2 = £240. Activity records confirm 120. Rate v2 gives 120 × £1.50 = £180, a £60 difference.
findings.evidenceObtained: Invoice line, matching 1–7 October activity records, signed rate v2 and obsolete v1 identify the rate error. CN82 records the agreed £60 credit.
findings.evidenceNeeded: None for this reconciled line and credit. Other invoice lines and VAT are outside the example.
findings.uncertainty: The fictional calculation excludes VAT and other lines. It establishes no external contract entitlement or wider ROI.
findings.possibleCause: Obsolete v1 rate was used instead of signed v2. The source of that rate-selection error is not established.
findings.nextAction: Commercial lead agrees CN82 for £60 on 8 October. Finance controller checks the credit and net £180 on the same day.
findings.urgency: Resolve this line within the 8 October commercial review. Service and storage questions remain separate.
findings.completion: 8 October 2026: commercial lead agrees £60 credit CN82. Finance controller verifies the resulting £180 net charge.
findings.verificationMethod: Reconcile the 120 pallet-days to signed rate v2 and check £240 invoice less £60 credit CN82 equals £180.
findings.verificationResult: Verified: net £180 agrees with 120 pallet-days at £1.50. The billing correction is closed for this line.
findings.decisionNeeded: Accept the verified credit for this line. Commercial lead checks contract timetable/options while the director awaits service and quality evidence.
findings.decisionOwner: Commercial lead for the credit; logistics director for the separate final renewal decision.

examples.managementNote: As at 8 October, the director awaits the quality assessment due 9 October and service plan due 10 October. Commercial lead checks contract timetable/options. The verified £60 credit does not settle renewal or product acceptability.

managementPrompts.label: Decision to make
managementPrompts.prompt: What decision is requested, and who has authority to make it?

managementPrompts.label: Scope and limits
managementPrompts.prompt: Which site, period, goods and sample support this brief? What was excluded?

managementPrompts.label: Findings and consequences
managementPrompts.prompt: What does the evidence establish, against which requirement, and what decision or activity does it affect?

managementPrompts.label: Open evidence and criteria
managementPrompts.prompt: What remains missing, uncertain or conflicting? What evidence could change the decision?

managementPrompts.label: User-flagged urgent concerns
managementPrompts.prompt: Record any concern the reviewer has flagged as urgent and its responsible response owner. Do not average it into an overall score.

managementPrompts.label: Options and resources
managementPrompts.prompt: What options are supported, what resources or approvals are needed, and what remains undecided?

managementPrompts.label: Decision and commitments
managementPrompts.prompt: Record the decision, rationale, action owners, target dates and any unresolved dependency.

managementPrompts.label: Follow-through
managementPrompts.prompt: Who checks effectiveness, using what evidence and when? What happens if the concern remains or returns?

findingPrompts.label: Finding and linked check
findingPrompts.prompt: Give the finding an ID and record the starter check ID or custom area.

findingPrompts.label: Criterion or reference
findingPrompts.prompt: What requirement applies? Record the relevant version or Not yet established.

findingPrompts.label: Observation and evidence
findingPrompts.prompt: What was observed, when and where? Add the record reference and sample.

findingPrompts.label: Evidence limits and possible cause
findingPrompts.prompt: What is uncertain? Keep a possible cause labelled as a hypothesis until evidence supports it.

findingPrompts.label: Consequence or decision affected
findingPrompts.prompt: Why does this finding matter within the stated review?

findingPrompts.label: Next action
findingPrompts.prompt: Specify correction, investigation, corrective action or verification; describe the next step.

findingPrompts.label: Owner and target date
findingPrompts.prompt: Who will do the work, by when? Leave an unassigned owner or unagreed date visible.

findingPrompts.label: Urgency assigned by reviewer
findingPrompts.prompt: Choose Not assessed, Routine follow-up or User-flagged urgent concern. Use the site's response process for an immediate concern.

findingPrompts.label: Decision or resources needed
findingPrompts.prompt: What prevents progress, who can resolve it and what decision is requested?

findingPrompts.label: Completion record
findingPrompts.prompt: What was completed, on what date and with which evidence?

findingPrompts.label: Effectiveness verification
findingPrompts.prompt: Record the method, reviewer, date, result and remaining limitations. Completion alone does not verify effectiveness.
